function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! 🎂 Where you’re located and what kind of cake you’re after really shape the best choices—but here’s a quick rundown of common ways people get fresh‑baked goodies delivered:

| Option | What it Offers | How to Order |
|--------|-----------------|--------------|
| **Local Artisan Bakeries** | Hand‑crafted flavors, seasonal ingredients, often customizable designs. | Search “bakery near me” on Google Maps/Yelp; many now accept orders through their own website or phone call. |
| **National Chains & Specialty Stores** | Consistent quality, wide variety (e.g., *Mrs. Fields*, *Bakeri*, *Cakes.com*). | Visit brand site → choose flavor/design → pick pickup/delivery time. |
| **Food‑Delivery Apps** *(UberEats, DoorDash, Grubhub)* | One‑stop shop—many independent bakers partner with them. | Browse the “Desserts/Cake” category, add to cart, checkout. |
| **Online Marketplaces** *(Amazon Fresh, Instacart)* | Same‑day grocery + dessert deliveries. | Add your favorite store’s selection to cart, schedule delivery window. |
| **Specialty Online Shops** *(Goldbelly, Cakes.com, Dessert Gallery)* | Gourmet, regional specialties shipped nationwide. | Pick a cake, customize details, ship directly to recipient. |
| **DIY Kits / Baking Subscription Boxes** *(Bakeology, King Arthur Flour Box)* | All‑in‑one kit delivered; great if you enjoy baking yourself. | Sign up on their site, select box size, receive ingredients & instructions. |

### Quick Tips for Ordering

1. **Know Your Occasion** – Some bakeries specialize in wedding cakes, birthdays, corporate events, etc.  
2. **Check Reviews & Photos** – Look for recent photos of finished cakes; taste ratings help too.  
3. **Ask About Customization** – Most places let you tweak frosting color, topper design, even gluten‑free or vegan fillings.  
4. **Order Early** – For special occasions, place orders 1–2 weeks in advance so the baker has enough prep time.  
5. **Confirm Delivery Window** – Make sure the cake arrives when you’ll actually be there to open it (or set a safe spot for overnight storage).

---

#### Need Help Narrowing Down?

If you tell me:
- City/state or zip code
- Budget range ($20–$200+)
- Any dietary needs (gluten‑free, dairy‑free, nut allergy, keto, etc.)
- Occasion (birthday, anniversary, office party)

I can suggest specific bakeries or online vendors that fit those criteria—and even pull up current deals or specials if you’d like!
